title: 1955 AHSME Problem 41
statement: A train traveling from Aytown to Beetown meets with an accident after \(1\) hr. It is stopped for \(\dfrac12\) hr., after which it proceeds at four-fifths of its usual rate, arriving at Beetown \(2\) hr. late. If the train had covered \(80\) miles more before the accident, it would have been just \(1\) hr. late. The usual rate of the train is:

solutions.text:
Let the usual rate be \(R\) mph and the total distance be \(D.\) After the first hour, the normal time for the remaining distance is \(\frac{D}{R}-1.\) Traveling it at \(\frac{4R}{5}\) adds one-fourth of that time, so \[ \frac12+\frac14\left(\frac DR-1\right)=2. \] If the accident occurs \(80\) miles later, \[ \frac12+\frac14\left(\frac DR-1-\frac{80}{R}\right)=1. \] Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \(\frac{20}{R}=1,\) hence \(R=20\) mph.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Traveling at \(\frac{4}{5}\) speed adds one-fourth of the normal time for the affected distance
Compare the two delays; moving the accident point \(80\) miles changes the delay by \(1\) hour
